A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same EC-Diffuser research work, including complete main text and Appendices A-D. Their text, equations, tables and figures support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original manipulation experiments, compositional generalization results, ablations and supplementary evaluations in Section 5 and Appendix D.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results, including benchmark comparisons, generalization experiments, ablations and Language-Table generation examples.

M1.justification: Sections 4.1-4.3 retain the same DLP encoding, entity-centric Transformer, joint state/action denoising, L1 objective and model-predictive control procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use PushCube, PushT, FrankaKitchen and Language-Table. Coverage of novel object counts, goal compositions, shapes and colors is unchanged, including Appendix D.

E2.justification: The corresponding comparisons retain VQ-BeT, Diffuser, EIT+BC and EC Diffusion Policy with unchanged participation. The newly cited Lin et al. work is not an evaluated baseline.

E3.justification: Evaluation settings remain identical, including 96 configurations for PushCube/PushT, 100 sampled FrankaKitchen goals, the 2700/300 Language-Table training/validation split and the training settings in Appendix C.

E4.justification: The representation, diffusion and state-generation ablations, temporal-attention analysis, alternative-input experiments and unseen-shape/color tests are unchanged in Sections 5.3-5.4 and Appendix D.

E5.justification: Both versions retain standard deviations across five seeds and the same temporal-attention T-test in Section 5.4. No repeated-run information or uncertainty-reporting practice changes.

E6.justification: All quantitative results and qualitative examples are unchanged. For example, Table 1 retains three-cube success of 0.894 ± 0.025, and Table 13 retains 3.340 ± 0.097 FrankaKitchen goals reached with Slot Attention.

T1.justification: The diffusion equations, representation definitions, architectural mathematics and training objectives in Sections 3-4 and Appendix A are unchanged. No theoretical results or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims about multi-object manipulation performance and zero-shot generalization to novel compositions and larger object counts.

C2.justification: Interpretations of joint state/action generation and the limitations concerning demonstration quality, object representations, diffusion inference time and unfamiliar object dynamics remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix C and Section 7 retain the same implementation details, hyperparameters, hardware and compute disclosures, data-processing information and code-access instructions.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds Lin et al. (2023b), 'Planning with spatial-temporal abstraction from point clouds for deformable object manipulation,' with a corresponding bibliography entry. The existing compositional-generalization survey becomes Lin et al. (2023a); the broader research positioning is unchanged.

P1.justification: Section 2 replaces 'methods that leverage object-centric representations' with the erroneous 'methods that e object-centric representations.' Citation labels and the arXiv version stamp also change, while the narrative and section organization remain intact.

P2.justification: The related-work paragraph rewraps, and bibliography reflow moves the Seitzer et al. reference from page 14 to page 15. Figures 1-16 and Tables 1-14 retain their content, structure and placement.

improvement.justification: The added related-work citation provides limited additional attribution, while the Section 2 typo slightly worsens wording. The scientific arguments, experimental evidence, appendices and reproducibility information remain unchanged, yielding no meaningful net difference in overall paper quality.
